answers.question: What does the company do and how does it earn money?

sentences.text: Shivalik Agro Polymers Ltd makes plastic films and pipes used in farming and irrigation.
It earned ₹640 crore in revenue in FY2026, up from ₹562.7 crore in FY2023.
Irrigation pipes accounts for 48.0% of revenue, the largest single business.
Over the last three years, revenue grew by 4.4% a year on average; the median for its Agricultural polymers peers is 9.0%.
Net profit shrank by 26.6% a year on average over the same period (peer median 6.0%) and was ₹7.7 crore in FY2026.
In FY2026 the company kept 7.0% of its revenue as operating profit (five-year median 8.2%, peer median 11.0%) and earned 2.2% on shareholders' money (peer median 10.5%).

answers.question: How is it priced against its own history and its peers?

sentences.text: The share price is 146.5x the yearly profit per share. That is above the company's own five-year median of 92.3x and above the peer median of 22.0x.
The share price is 3.2x the shareholders' money per share (book value), below its own five-year median of 4.1x and above the peer median of 2.4x.
The whole company is valued at ₹1,150 crore on the market, against ₹1,093 crore a year ago, and its dividend yield is 0.0% (peer median 0.5%).
